items.title: Meta declined a UK watchdog's offer to test Muse before launch
items.summary: WIRED reports that Meta turned down a Financial Conduct Authority suggestion to test Muse together in the regulator's sandbox before the UK rollout. Colin Payne, the FCA's head of innovation, said the agency wants to see how the agent handles payments and whether it acts for the customer. Meta said it has engaged with the relevant regulators. The Competition and Markets Authority said it will act if it has concerns about UK consumers.

items.title: Gap uses Cognition's Devin to keep holiday shopping online
items.summary: Gap Inc. said on 25 November 2026 that engineers use Cognition's Devin agent on its ecommerce sites. A daily site scan looks for shopper friction and system faults, then drafts a tested code fix for a person to review and publish. Gap says that work has helped recover millions in sales that downtime would have lost, and that people still approve every change.

items.title: Human Security sees AI agent traffic heading for a 150x Cyber Week
items.summary: Adweek reports that Human Security expects AI agent traffic during Cyber Week, 26 to 30 November, to reach about 150 times last year's level, with checkout-page requests near 160 times. Meta's Muse accounts for about 70 percent of the agent traffic Human sees and 57 percent of checkout requests. The figures count page and search actions on sites Human protects, not completed orders.

items.title: Amazon and Meta reportedly in talks to lift blockade on AI agent Muse
items.summary: TechCrunch reports that Amazon and Meta have held talks about letting Muse shop on Amazon, according to Fortune. The open questions are how search results would appear and how advertising would work, and any deal would need both chief executives to approve it. Two months ago, Muse shoppers could not check out on Amazon. Neither company had commented.

items.title: Duco opens an MCP server for post-trade reconciliation agents
items.summary: Duco made its MCP server generally available on 25 November 2026. Agents on any MCP client can search reconciliation breaks, label them, and match or clear exceptions under the user's existing permissions. Every action is written to Duco's audit log, and the server is available to Duco clients.

items.title: Alta opens an MCP server so sales agents can prospect in chat
items.summary: Alta opened Alta MCP in Claude, ChatGPT, and Codex on 25 November 2026. A rep can describe an audience, get verified contacts, and draft a multichannel campaign in the same chat. Campaigns stay drafts until a person launches them, and sending or resuming a campaign asks for confirmation first.

items.title: Magister opens a marketing MCP server across 85 tools
items.summary: Magister Marketing launched an MCP server on 25 November 2026 that connects Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor, and other MCP clients to 85 marketing tools. It can read analytics and ad accounts and draft posts, but anything that publishes, sends, or spends waits for a person to approve it. Connect is $29 a month and the Agent plan is $99 a month, after a free trial.

items.title: Google Workspace opens MCP servers and a CLI for governed AI agents
items.summary: Google made Workspace MCP servers and a Workspace CLI generally available, giving agents a managed way into Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, and other Workspace apps. A new addendum tells agents to use those doors instead of REST APIs, with technical enforcement starting 1 February 2027. Admins can require confirmations, read audit logs, and revoke access.
